title: Review annotations to GO:0000032 cell wall mannoprotein biosynthetic process GO:0031506 cell wall glycoprotein biosynthetic process

author: pgaudet
body:
Annotations are from CGD (13), SGD (19) and 1 from Pombase. 

@suzialeksander @jlewsmith @ValWood 
Would you be OK to replace these with (possibly): [protein O-linked mannosylation](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_0035269)

author: pgaudet
source_title: Obsoletion request: GO:0000032 cell wall mannoprotein biosynthetic process/ GO:0031506   cell wall glycoprotein biosynthetic process

author: ValWood
body:
It is difficult for curators to remember when concurrent annotations are required.

The problem that needs to be resolved is:

i)  these terms are in their own branch and not related to the appropriate 
protein X-linked pathways.
ii) the terms are only differentiated by location, rather than by process

Could we perhaps instead have subclasses to capture these pathways?

N-linked mannosylation, cell wall biogenesis 
O-linked mannosylation, cell wall biogenesis 
(with better term labels: can we even use "N-linked mannosylation involved in  cell wall biogenesis" since we aren' linking a MF to a BP?)

would this work instead? 

(Also, have been meaning to mention that we shouldn't really require fungal-type and plant-type cell wall terms- if the term isn't relevant for a species this can be dealt with by taxon restrictions- this would be a nice simplification)

author: pgaudet
body: It seems that these terms are not at the same level: x synthesis pathway versus organelle organization, and should be co-annotated rather than pre-composed.

author: ValWood
body:
But this would be 2 different ways of describing the same process. It isn't 2 different processes.

In this case  either the O-linked mannosylation, is part of cell wall biogenesis, or it is causally upstream of it?

Where does cell wall biogenesis begin?
it is defined
A cellular process that results in the biosynthesis of constituent macromolecules, assembly, and arrangement of constituent parts of a cell wall. Includes biosynthesis of constituent macromolecules, such as proteins and polysaccharides, and those macromolecular modifications that are involved in synthesis or assembly of the cellular component. A cell wall is the rigid or semi-rigid envelope lying outside the cell membrane of plant, fungal and most prokaryotic cells, maintaining their shape and protecting them from osmotic lysis.

So, as defined, biogenesis includes biosynthesis of constituent macromolecules?


These  "biogenesis" terms are quite problematic because they implicity cover upstream synthesis events

Underneath biogenesis we have terms like

GO:0070726   cell wall assembly
which are specific to the events at the cell surface.

Now we have GO-CAM we could do without the biogenesis terms (IMHO)
because the glycoprotein formation can be modelled as upstream processes.

author: pgaudet
body:
> These "biogenesis" terms are quite problematic because they implicity cover upstream synthesis events

Exactly. We should just have 'cell wall assembly'.

author: ValWood
body:
In that case it makes sense to annotate to only
N-linked/O-linked  mannosylation pending the future changes.
